newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian street protests claim first victim.
newsitem.headline: Albanian street protests claim first victim.

text.p: Weeks of protests against Albania's right-wing government by investors who lost their life savings in shady investment schemes have claimed their first fatality.
The Health Ministry said one person died and 23 were injured when demonstrators threw stones at a police station in the Adriatic port of Vlore on Sunday and police responded by firing into the air.
The violence, a day after riot police used batons to prevent demonstrators from massing in central Tirana, was sparked by rumours that people had been arrested.
Tens of thousands of protesters denouncing President Sali Berisha had marched through Vlore for five days in a row without incident after police gave up trying to disperse them.

Leaders of the 10 parties in the opposition Forum for Democracy alliance planned to meet on Monday to assess the weekend's events and consider an invitation from Berisha's Democratic Party to fresh talks on failed investment schemes.

"Our president is irresponsible. If you close the way to dialogue people get more desperate. I am afraid of civil war," Neritan Ceka, leader of the centre-right Democratic Alliance party, told Reuters Television.
"Europe must be more aware and treat Albania with the same standards as Belgrade. Otherwise it is not honest."
Ceka was earlier attacked in a Tirana cafe by men in khaki uniforms whom he said had been hired by Berisha's party. The Interior Ministry denied involvement.

The Forum wants talks with Berisha but turned down an invitation last week, saying it was a "publcity stunt". It says restrictions on rallies make it harder for the opposition to confront authorities than in Bulgaria or Serbia, where mass demonstrations have won government concessions.

After riot police aborted its rally on Saturday, the Forum changed tactics, urging supporters to try to shut down Tirana at lunch time every day by closing shops, boycotting classes and marching through streets with a slice of bread.
Berisha, shown on state television meeting local leaders from Vlore before the clashes there, repeated that anyone violating Albania's laws would be punished.
He urged Albanians to turn away from people "who resort to violence and demand the government's resignation but offer no solutions."
Hospital officials said the victim of Sunday's clash died of a heart attack. Demonstrators said he was covered in blood when taken to hospital and blamed police for his death.
The officials said many of the injured had minor buckshot wounds and one person was in intensive care. State television said 12 policemen were also injured, one by a petrol bomb.

Demonstrators had marched in now standard fashion through Vlore and later set wrecked cars on fire. Some erected roadblocks on the main road linking the city with Tirana to prevent police reinforcements from arriving.

Widespread rioting swept Albania last month after pyramid schemes offering quick returns started to go bust. The schemes had attracted money from virtually every family in the country of 3.4 million people in the six years since the overthrow of communism.

Fresh disturbances erupted last week after a pyramid scheme based in Vlore went bankrupt owing investors some $500 million. Economists believe as much as $2 billion may be tied up in all the schemes and say new collapses are inevitable.
